title: Portable handoff, stage 1: Git push, clean release and returning pull
outcome: Deferred runtime delivery of the first Git handoff proposal after final design concurrence and coordinator scheduling: one project moves A-to-B-to-A with one active writer, native shared history and frozen old stores. User resumed design work, not live-store cutover. Required format conversion and migration go to Greg before live installation.
acceptance: A representative project in disposable repository homes executes manual push, release A, pull B, mutate shared work/memory, release B, and returning pull A. Exactly one writer can mutate throughout, both prior released stores remain preserved, imported full/closure checks pass, and native completed items retain original seals/evidence/ids rather than graph-import completions.
Two homes that acquire the same released head end with exactly one `active` store, and the other is refused with `portable_diverged` and has enabled nothing; a test in the repository shows it
A portable store restored from a backup copy is frozen with `portable_instance_missing`, and a `local` project's words behave as before with no target configured; tests in the repository show both

docs/shipped.md has a row for each shipped portable word, docs/features/portable-handoff.md marks stage 1 as shipped, and the changeset that adds the writer record teaches `migration import` the conversion and names it in its report

The complete first-version contract includes exact-head Git conformance, useful payload closure, Windows installation crash/namespace durability evidence and demonstrated host admission/drain/identity behavior. No first-version takeover, detach, automatic scheduling or simultaneous cross-host writers; no real deployment claim without the separately approved live-store conversion and actual two-machine exercise.
disposal_reason: Portable handoff was replaced before any of it shipped: docs/features/git-task-sync.md says the previous portable writer-epoch and release/acquire design is gone, AGENTS.md says the selected sync uses no global writer lock, writer epochs or release/acquire protocol, and master has no portable code or brief. Its six children are rejected. Cancelled under Greg's word, 43498a6e #683. Nothing here was built or tested.
